H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H3117: a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb)
H7227: abundant (in quantity, size, age, number, rank, quality)
H310: properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses)
H834: who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc.
H5117: to rest, i.e. settle down; used in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, intransitive, transitive and causative (to dwell, stay, let fall, place, let alone, withdraw, give comfort, etc.)
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H3478: Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H5439: (as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around
H935: to go or come (in a wide variety of applications)
H7121: to call out to (i.e. properly, address by name, but used in a wide variety of applications)
H7218: the head (as most easily shaken), whether literal or figurative (in many applications, of place, time, rank, itc.)
H8199: to judge, i.e. pronounce sentence (for or against); by implication, to vindicate or punish; by extenssion, to govern; passively, to litigate (literally or figuratively)
H7860: properly, a scribe, i.e. (by analogy or implication) an official superintendent or magistrate
H413: near, with or among; often in general, to
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H7200: to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
H853: properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely)
H6213: to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H1471: a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts
H6440: the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H1931: he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are
H3898: to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction)
H5307: to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative)
H7604: properly, to swell up, i.e. be (causatively, make) redundant
H5159: properly, something inherited, i.e. (abstractly) occupancy, or (concretely) an heirloom; generally an estate, patrimony or portion
H7626: a scion, i.e. (literally) a stick (for punishing, writing, fighting, ruling, walking, etc.) or (figuratively) a clan
H4480: properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses
H3383: Jarden, the principal river of Palestine
H3772: to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces)
H3220: a sea (as breaking in noisy surf) or large body of water; specifically (with the article), the Mediterranean Sea; sometimes a large river, or an artifical basin; locally, the west, or (rarely) the south
H1419: great (in any sense); hence, older; also insolent
H3996: an entrance (the place or the act); specifically sunset or the west; also (adverb with preposition) towards
H8121: the sun; by implication, the east; figuratively, a ray, i.e. (architectural) a notched battlement
H3423: to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H1696: perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue
H2388: to fasten upon; hence, to seize, be strong (figuratively, courageous, causatively strengthen, cure, help, repair, fortify), obstinate; to bind, restrain, conquer
H3966: properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated)
H8104: properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc.
H3789: to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe)
H5612: properly, writing (the art or a document); by implication, a book
H8451: a precept or statute, especially the Decalogue or Pentateuch
H1115: properly, a failure of, i.e. (used only as a negative particle, usually with a prepositional prefix) not, except, without, unless, besides, because not, until, etc.
H3225: the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south
H8040: properly, dark (as enveloped), i.e. the north; hence (by orientation), the left hand
H854: properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc.
H8034: an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H2142: properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention; to be male
H7650: to seven oneself, i.e. swear (as if by repeating a declaration seven times)
H5647: to work (in any sense); by implication, to serve, till, (causatively) enslave, etc.
H7812: to depress, i.e. prostrate (especially reflexive, in homage to royalty or God)
H518: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not
H1692: properly, to impinge, i.e. cling or adhere; figuratively, to catch by pursuit
H5704: as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with)
H2088: the masculine demonstrative pronoun, this or that
H6099: powerful (specifically, a paw); by implication, numerous
H5975: to stand, in various relations (literal and figurative, intransitive and transitive)
H376: a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
H259: properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first
H7291: to run after (usually with hostile intent; figuratively (of time) gone by)
H505: hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand
H5315: properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental)
H157: to have affection for (sexually or otherwise)
H7725: to turn back (hence, away) transitively or intransitively, literally or figuratively (not necessarily with the idea of return to the starting point); generally to retreat; often adverbial, again
H3499: properly, an overhanging, i.e. (by implication) an excess, superiority, remainder; also a small rope (as hanging free)
H2859: to give (a daughter) away in marriage; hence (generally) to contract affinity by marriage
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H3254: to add or augment (often adverbial, to continue to do a thing)
H6341: a (metallic) sheet (as pounded thin); also a spring net (as spread out like a lamina)
H4170: a noose (for catching animals) (literally or figuratively); by implication, a hook (for the nose)
H5869: an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape)
H6: properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H2896: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
H5414: to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)
H1980: to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
H1870: a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
H3824: the heart (as the most interior organ);
H1697: a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause
H3651: properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles)
H7451: bad or (as noun) evil (natural or moral)
H5674: to cross over; used very widely of any transition (literal or figurative; transitive, intransitive, intensive, causative); specifically, to cover (in copulation)
H1285: a compact (because made by passing between pieces of flesh)
H312: properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc.
H2734: to glow or grow warm; figuratively (usually) to blaze up, of anger, zeal, jealousy
H639: properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire
